# Takumi Motion — full documentation

> Deterministic server-side animation engine: React or HTML -> GIF/WebP/APNG/PNG-sequence/sprite-sheet/still, rendered by the Rust takumi engine.

## Tutorials

Guided walkthroughs for first-time users.

### Declarative Banners
Source: /tutorials/declarative-banners

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard, Steps, TabItem, Tabs } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Not every banner needs a component tree. Takumi Motion ships four deterministic banner recipes — `typewriter`, `countup`, `sweep`, and `cascade` — plus a declarative timeline API. In this tutorial you render a template-based banner from a plain TypeScript file, then emit the full multi-preset asset kit.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 22 or later
- `takumi-motion` installed (see [Your First Banner](/tutorials/first-banner) for installation)

## 1. Render a template

Templates are functions that return a `BannerResult` — an element plus a compiled-ready timeline. Create `release-banner.ts`:

<Code lang="ts" code={`import { gradientSweepBanner, renderBanner } from "takumi-motion";

const result = await gradientSweepBanner({
    title: "v2.4 — no more cold starts",
    subtitle: "cold starts down 96%",
    theme: "dracula",
});

const report = await renderBanner({
    node: result.element,
    timeline: result.timeline,
    preset: "readme",
    outDir: "./out",
    baseName: "release",
});

console.log(report.totalBytes, report.overBudget);`} />

Run it:

<Code lang="sh" code={`node release-banner.ts`} />

You get `./out/release.gif` and `./out/release.webp` plus a poster PNG. The template bakes a strict loop seam, so the animation repeats without a visible cut.

## 2. Understand the shared template props

All four templates share the same option vocabulary (`TemplateStyleProps`):

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` | `"midnight"` | Color theme name or partial theme object |
| `motion` | `"snappy" \| "smooth" \| "playful" \| "mechanical"` | template default | Personality preset driving easing and stagger |
| `font` | `FontSpec` | theme default | Google Font name or spec |
| `width` / `height` | `number` | 850 / 200 | Logical canvas size in pixels |
| `fps` | `number` | 20 | Frames per second of the baked timeline |
| `renderer` | `TakumiRenderer` | shared renderer | Pre-built renderer instance for reuse |

Each template adds its own props — for example `typewriter` takes `text`, `tagline`, and `speed` (milliseconds per character); `countup` takes a `stats` array of `{ label, value, suffix?, decimals? }`. The full signatures live in [Presets, Themes & Fonts](/reference/presets-and-themes#banner-templates).

## 3. Use the CLI for one-off renders

The `render` command loads a module and renders whatever it exports — a template result, an element-plus-timeline object, or a sync/async function returning either. Create `banner-cli.ts`:

<Code lang="ts" code={`import { cascadeBanner } from "takumi-motion/recipes";

export default await cascadeBanner({
    title: "takumi-motion",
    tagline: "deterministic banners from code",
    accent: "#DF4D24",
});`} />

Then render it from the terminal:

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="pnpm">
<Code lang="sh" code={` pnpm exec takumi-motion render banner-cli.ts --preset readme-wide --out ./out`} />
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="npx">
<Code lang="sh" code={` npx takumi-motion render banner-cli.ts --preset readme-wide --out ./out`} />
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

The loader resolves, in order: the module's default export, a `banner` export, then an `element` export. It accepts React elements, `defineBanner` functions, and `{ element, timeline }` template results alike.

## 4. Emit the full asset kit

The `--kit` flag renders a banner across several presets plus a static reduced-motion twin — the complete asset set for a project README:

<Code lang="sh" code={`pnpm exec takumi-motion render banner-cli.ts --kit --out ./assets`} />

Programmatically, the same call is `renderKit`:

<Code lang="ts" code={`import { renderKit } from "takumi-motion";

const kit = await renderKit(bannerResult, { outDir: "./assets" });
console.log(kit.files); // [{ path, role }, ...]`} />

The kit writes `<base>-<preset>.<ext>` files for the `readme`, `readme-hd`, and `readme-lean` presets, plus `banner-static.png`. The CLI exits with code 2 when any variant exceeds its preset's byte budget.

<Aside type="caution">
  `--kit` supports declarative banners only. The React path prints a warning and renders normally.
</Aside>

## 5. Author a custom timeline

When templates do not fit, build a timeline directly. `createTimeline` mirrors Motion's API — targets, keyframes, transitions — and renderers consume its JSON form. Timeline JSON is the interchange format every render path accepts:

<Code lang="ts" code={`import { createTimeline, renderBanner, h } from "takumi-motion";

const node = h("div", { style: { fontSize: 42, fontWeight: 700 } }, "ship it");

const timeline = createTimeline({ fps: 20 }).add(
    node,
    { opacity: [0, 1], y: [-24, 0] },
    { at: 0, duration: 600 },
);

const report = await renderBanner({
    node,
    timeline: timeline.toJSON(),
    outDir: "./out",
});`} />

`renderBanner` runs `compileTimeline` internally — bake it yourself only when you need the CSS output for inspection. Timeline transforms (`shiftTimeline`, `concatTimelines`) compose longer sequences declaratively — the data equivalent of stacking scenes.

## Next steps

### Your First Banner
Source: /tutorials/first-banner

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard, Steps, TabItem, Tabs } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

In this tutorial you build and render a React banner — the golden path for producing an animated README badge or OG card. You install the package, define scenes, render server-side to WebP, and read the render report. The whole walkthrough takes about fifteen minutes.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 22 or later
- pnpm 10 or later
- Basic familiarity with React function components

## 1. Create a project and install

Create an empty directory and initialize a package:

<Code lang="sh" code={`mkdir my-banner && cd my-banner
pnpm init`} />

Install `takumi-motion`:

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="pnpm">
<Code lang="sh" code={` pnpm add takumi-motion`} />
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="npm">
<Code lang="sh" code={` npm add takumi-motion`} />
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="yarn">
<Code lang="sh" code={` yarn add takumi-motion`} />
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

<Aside type="note">
  The package ships its own TypeScript execution path (`tsx`), so you do not need a bundler or a build config to render banners from `.tsx` files.
</Aside>

## 2. Define a banner

A banner is a React component wrapped in `defineBanner`. Inside it, a `<Banner>` element declares the surface and theme, and `<Scene>` elements declare what plays and for how long. Duration units are **frames**, not seconds.

Create a file named `launch-banner.tsx`:

<Code lang="tsx" code={`import { defineBanner, Banner, Scene, Layer } from "takumi-motion/react";
import { renderReactBanner } from "takumi-motion";

export const launchBanner = defineBanner(function TakumiMotionLaunch() {
        return (
    <Banner preset="readme" theme="tokyo-night" transitionMs={250}>
            <Layer bottom>
                    <div
                            style={{
                                    position: "absolute",
                                    bottom: 0,
                                    width: 850,
                                    height: 3,
                                    backgroundColor: "#7aa2f7",
                            }}
                    />
            </Layer>

            <Scene duration={100} enter="rise" exit="crossfade">
                    <h1 style={{ fontSize: 48, fontWeight: 700, color: "#c0caf5" }}>
                            takumi-motion
                    </h1>
            </Scene>
    </Banner>
        );
});

const report = await renderReactBanner({
        banner: launchBanner,
        formats: ["webp"],
        outDir: "./out",
});

console.log(report.lint);`} />

<Aside type="caution">
  Pass `formats` (an array) and `outDir` (a directory), not `format` or a file path. The renderer picks file names from the preset and base name.
</Aside>

Three details carry the design:

- `preset="readme"` selects the 850×200 @ 20 fps surface with a 2 MiB budget (see [Presets, Themes & Fonts](/reference/presets-and-themes)).
- `<Scene duration={100}>` means 100 frames — five seconds at the preset's 20 fps.
- `<Layer bottom>` keeps the accent rule pinned beneath the animated text.

## 3. Render it

Run the file with Node:

<Code lang="sh" code={`node launch-banner.tsx`} />

The command prints a report and writes `./out/launch-banner.webp`:

<Code lang="json" code={`{
  "format": "webp",
  "bytes": 184320,
  "withinBudget": true
}`} />

Open the file in a browser — you see the title rise in, hold, and crossfade out. The same bytes render on every machine and every run.

## 4. Read the report

`renderReactBanner` returns a `ReactBannerReport`. The fields you reach for most:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `files` | Written or buffered outputs: path, format, byte count, per-file budget verdict |
| `lint` | Coded authoring warnings (`TM_*`), deduplicated, with fix hints |
| `seam` | Loop-seam verdict (`mode: "exact"` when frame 0 equals the final frame) |
| `timings` | Milliseconds spent in capture, parse, audit, and encode stages |

A non-empty `report.lint` does not fail the render. It tells you what will cost bytes or break layout — for example `TM_KEBAB_STYLE` when a style object uses kebab-case keys that the engine rejects. See [Lint Codes](/reference/lint-codes) for the full table.

## 5. Try the CLI

The same banner renders from the terminal without writing a driver script:

<Code lang="sh" code={`npx takumi-motion render launch-banner.tsx --out ./out`} />

The CLI accepts `--format gif,webp`, `--budget 800000`, `--filmstrip`, and more — every flag is documented in the [CLI reference](/reference/cli).

## How-to Guides

Task-oriented recipes for specific goals.

### CI Quality Gates
Source: /guides/ci-quality-gates

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Use this guide to make broken banners unshippable. Two tools cover the gates: the `check` CLI command for fast, local-style verification, and `renderWithAudit` for a full determinism-probing audit as data.

## Exit codes you can gate on

| Tool | Exit | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `takumi-motion check` | `0` | Extents, seam, and sizes pass — "OK — ship it" |
| `takumi-motion check` | `1` | A non-decorative extent violation, a seam that differs on a declared loop, or a size over budget — "FAILED — do not ship" |
| `takumi-motion render --budget N` | `2` | Output exceeded the byte budget after the fps ladder ran |
| `renderWithAudit()` | `0` / `1` / `2` | Pass / content failure (extent hard-fail) / over budget |

The `check` command renders the banner once and audits it. With `--out` it also writes the preset's formats and checks their sizes; without it, the audit runs render-free of file output.

## Add a GitHub Actions gate

<Code lang="github-actions" code={`name: banner-quality
on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  banners:
 runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 steps:
   - uses: actions/checkout@v4
   - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
   - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
     with:
       node-version: 22
       cache: pnpm
   - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
   - name: Check banners
     run: |
       pnpm exec takumi-motion check src/banners/readme.tsx
       pnpm exec takumi-motion check src/banners/og.tsx --budget 3000000
   - name: Render artifact on failure for review
     if: failure()
     run: pnpm exec takumi-motion render src/banners/readme.tsx --out ./out`} />

The failed run leaves the rendered files in `./out` for upload as an artifact, so reviewers see exactly what tripped the gate.

## What `check` audits

- **Extents** — the measured element tree is re-walked with fine-grid transform sampling; any box that leaves the canvas safe zone fails when it is not decorative (glow and ambient layers warn instead).
- **Loop seam** — a declared `loop` must report a matching seam; strict-mode seam energy above 0.02 fails the declarative path.
- **Sizes** — with `--out`, each written file's byte count is compared against its budget.

## Audit as data: `renderWithAudit`

Embed the same guarantees in your own pipeline. `renderWithAudit` renders, audits, and returns everything as JSON:

<Code lang="ts" code={`import { renderWithAudit } from "takumi-motion/audit";

const { report, audit, exitCode, formatted } = await renderWithAudit({
    banner: MyBanner,
    preset: "readme",
    budgetBytes: 2 * 1024 * 1024,
    outDir: "./out",
});

if (exitCode !== 0) {
    console.error(formatted);
    process.exit(exitCode);
}`} />

The `audit` object contains `budget` (per-file verdicts), `extents` (violations with frame, target, edge, overflow), `seam`, `warnings`, and a `determinism` block — a full second render with a byte comparison of the first poster. Treat `audit.deterministic === false` as a hard alarm: it means the pipeline lost purity somewhere (a `Math.random` outside the shim, a clock read, a network fetch).

<Aside type="tip">
  `renderWithAudit` lives behind the `takumi-motion/audit` subpath export — a deliberate embeddability contract for platforms that render user banners.
</Aside>

### Data-Driven Animations
Source: /guides/data-driven-animations

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Use this guide when a banner needs to visualize numbers — stars, revenue, latency, coverage. The data channel injects one JSON object at setup; nothing is fetched while frames render, which is what keeps the output byte-reproducible.

## The rule: data enters at setup, never at render

A network fetch inside a render function is a determinism violation. File reads are fine — they are immutable inputs. Pass data programmatically or through the CLI:

<Code lang="ts" code={`const report = await renderReactBanner({
    banner: MetricsReel,
    data: metricsJson,
});`} />

<Code lang="sh" code={`npx takumi-motion render metrics-reel.tsx --data metrics.json --format webp`} />

Inside the component tree, read the object anywhere with `useChartData`:

<Code lang="tsx" code={`import { useChartData } from "takumi-motion/react";

function Headline() {
    const data = useChartData<{ stars: number }>();
    return <span>{data.stars.toLocaleString("en-US")} stars</span>;
}`} />

`useChartData(hint?)` throws with a hint listing registered keys when no channel exists; call `hasChartData()` when you need a quiet check.

## Render a line chart

`<LineChart>` builds one static SVG, then sweeps a per-frame `clip-path: inset()` across it — that clip reveal is the draw engine:

<Code lang="tsx" code={`<LineChart
    data={{ series: [{ name: "rps", color: "#7aa2f7", points: [12, 30, 28, 55, 61, 80] }], labels: ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar"] }}
    draw="reveal"
    area
    grid
    showPoints
/>`} />

Key props: `draw="none"` renders the finished chart (use it for stills), `drawDurationFrames`/`drawDelayFrames` control the sweep, and `yTicks` sets gridline density. Data can arrive via props or the channel — omit the `data` prop and the chart reads `useChartData` itself.

## Render bars and donuts

`<BarChart>` grows bars with staggered closed-form springs; `<Donut>` sweeps a value arc:

<Code lang="tsx" code={`<BarChart
    data={{ series: [{ name: "downloads", color: "#DF4D24", points: [820, 1240, 980, 1610] }] }}
    orientation="up"
    stagger
    showValues
/>

<Donut value={0.83} size={140} color="#7aa2f7">
    <span style={{ fontSize: 24 }}>83%</span>
</Donut>`} />

`<Donut>` validates `value` in the `[0, 1]` range. The default `paint="transform"` sweep is palette-safe for GIF; `paint="conic"` is the gradient alternative but trips the GIF dither lint on 1× surfaces.

## Count up with stable digit columns

`<CountUp>` accepts a `format` pattern — parsed once, rendered with `tabular-nums` forced on, so digit columns never reflow siblings:

<Code lang="tsx" code={`<CountUp to={4200} durationFrames={40} delayFrames={6} format="$,.0f" />
<CountUp to={0.962} format=",.1f%" />
<CountUp to={37} format="ms" />`} />

Pattern grammar: `[prefix][, grouping][.Nf decimals][suffix]`. Function formers still work: `format={(v) => \`${Math.round(v).toLocaleString("en-US")}+ stars\`}`.

<Aside type="caution">
  Counting digits change width every frame. Without `tabular-nums` (applied automatically) or `minWidth` on custom layouts, neighboring elements shift and trip `TM_LAYOUT_SHIFT`.
</Aside>

<LinkCard title="Reduce File Size" href="/guides/reduce-file-size" description="Count-up churn is WebP territory — read the report and act on it." />

### Parallel Capture
Source: /guides/parallel-capture

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Frame capture is embarrassingly parallel — each frame is a pure function of `(frame, props)` — so heavy banners render across worker threads. Use this guide when capture dominates your render time (large canvases, hundreds of frames, deep trees).

## Switch to module mode

Parallel capture requires the banner to be addressable as a module, because each worker imports it independently. Pass `bannerModule` instead of `banner`:

<Code lang="ts" code={`import { renderReactBanner } from "takumi-motion";

const report = await renderReactBanner({
    bannerModule: "./launch-banner.tsx", // the file's default export
    workers: "auto",
    formats: ["webp"],
    outDir: "./out",
});`} />

The module path's default export can be a React element, a `defineBanner` component, or a function returning either. The CLI equivalent is `--workers auto` (module banners only).

## Let the auto gate decide

`workers: "auto"` refuses to spawn unless the host actually benefits:

| Condition | Threshold |
| --- | --- |
| Available cores | ≥ 4 |
| Banner length | ≥ 128 frames |
| Measured capture work | ≥ 400 ms (probe-timed) |

The main thread probes once — two static renders establish the plan and per-frame cost — and only then spawns up to 16 workers over a window grid. On smaller hosts the Rust stages already saturate the machine, and spawning JS workers oversubscribes it; the bench table in the repository records a real case where `workers: 4` on a 2-core host measured 0.88× (slower). The gate keeps serial there.

A numeric `workers: 4` forces the pool (capped at 16 and at the frame count) when you know better than the gate.

<Aside type="tip">
  Byte-identity holds at **any** worker count — windows are concatenated and re-chunked once, plan agreement is asserted before merge, and the frame-seeded PRNG shim makes each frame's render a pure function of `(frame, props)`. Golden tests in the repository assert this invariant; you can assert it too by diffing serial and parallel outputs.
</Aside>

## Render frame windows

Debug a range without re-rendering everything:

<Code lang="ts" code={`const report = await renderReactBanner({
    bannerModule: "./reel.tsx",
    fromFrame: 120,
    toFrame: 180,
});`} />

The CLI pair is `--from 120 --to 180`. The report's `window` block records the range that ran.

## Estimate before you commit

The report's `timings` block splits capture, parse, audit, and encode. If `captureMs` is small next to `encodeMs`, more workers will not help — move to [Reduce File Size](/guides/reduce-file-size) instead.

### Preview and Inspect
Source: /guides/preview-and-inspect

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard, TabItem, Tabs } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Four inspection tools ship with the engine. They answer different questions — picking the right one saves render cycles.

## The tools at a glance

| Tool | What you get | Source of truth | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--filmstrip` | N engine-exact stills in one self-contained HTML | The actual shipped pixels | Review diffs — output is byte-deterministic |
| `preview` | A playable HTML of the captured CSS | Approximate layout | Scrubbing motion timing |
| `storyboard` | A labeled PNG contact sheet of the timeline | Engine-rasterized cells | Whole-timeline visual QA |
| `renderStill` | One PNG frame | Engine-exact | Link previews, avatars, golden frames |

## Engine-exact filmstrip

Every cell is rendered by the Rust engine — what you review is what you ship:

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="6 evenly spaced frames">
<Code lang="sh" code={` npx takumi-motion render banner.tsx --filmstrip`} />
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Explicit frames">
<Code lang="sh" code={` npx takumi-motion render banner.tsx --filmstrip 0,15,30`} />
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="10 frames">
<Code lang="sh" code={` npx takumi-motion render banner.tsx --filmstrip 10`} />
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

The filmstrip is self-contained HTML and byte-deterministic, so it diffs cleanly in pull requests. Programmatic form: `renderFilmstrip` (root export) — accepts react banners, HTML sources, and declarative node+timeline alike.

## CSS preview player

<Code lang="sh" code={`npx takumi-motion preview banner.tsx -o banner-preview.html`} />

The player replays the captured CSS in a browser — good for feeling the motion, approximate for layout. The encoded GIF/WebP remains the source of truth; when they disagree, trust the encoded output.

## Storyboard contact sheet

The storyboard renders a labeled PNG grid of the whole timeline (cells rasterized by the engine — the sheet itself is a takumi document) plus a sidecar JSON with the sampled frame indices:

<Code lang="sh" code={`npx takumi-motion storyboard reel.tsx --frames 12 --columns 4 --out ./qa`} />

Use it to review scene order, transitions, and seam behavior at a glance. Programmatic form: `renderStoryboard` with `{ banner, frames, columns, scale }`.

## Single stills

<Code lang="sh" code={`npx takumi-motion render banner.tsx --still        # settled frame (~60% of the timeline)
npx takumi-motion render banner.tsx --still 0      # explicit frame`} />

Looping banners poster and still default to frame 0 — the landing frame. `renderStill` returns `{ png, bytes, path }` and supports all three source paths.

<Aside type="tip">
  Pair the filmstrip with `--explain`: the filmstrip shows which frames exist, the X-ray shows why each one exists. Together they localize size waste in one pass.
</Aside>

### Reduce File Size
Source: /guides/reduce-file-size

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Encoded size is per-frame delta × frames. Everything in this guide attacks one of those two terms. Start from the report — it tells you which term dominates.

## 1. Set a budget and let the fps ladder work

The CLI accepts a byte budget and negotiates frame rate for you:

<Code lang="sh" code={`npx takumi-motion render banner.tsx --budget 800000 --out ./out`} />

When the first render exceeds the budget, the ladder re-renders at 75%, then 50% of the fps (floor 6 fps, first preset format) and keeps the first attempt that fits. The CLI exits `2` when even the ladder fails — wire that into CI as described in [Quality Gates](/guides/ci-quality-gates). Programmatically the same ladder is `optimizeBudget` from the root export.

## 2. Read the X-ray before guessing

`--explain` (or `explain: true` on `renderReactBanner`) attaches per-frame attribution to `report.explain`: every frame is classified as a start, hold, or change, and each change is attributed to a channel — opacity, transform, clip, layout, paint, text, or structure:

<Code lang="sh" code={`npx takumi-motion render banner.tsx --explain --json | jq .explain.summary`} />

<Code lang="json" code={`{
  "totalFrames": 180,
  "uniqueFrames": 96,
  "holds": 84,
  "cheapFrames": 52,
  "churnFrames": 44,
  "churnRanges": [{ "from": 60, "to": 104 }]
}`} />

Cheap frames (opacity, clip) compress well. Churn frames (layout, text, structure) re-encode whole regions — a churn range in the middle of a static scene is your first target.

## 3. Apply the doctrine fixes

- **Prefer WebP for glow and color sweeps.** Palette dithering of soft gradients is the leading GIF size trap — 1× glow GIFs compressed worse than 2× in the project benchmarks. The `TM_GLOW_GIF_DITHER` lint fires on `filter: blur()` at dpr 1 into GIF.
- **Let holds collapse.** Settled animation descriptors emit no style overrides, so identical frames merge into zero-delta holds — the GIF pass rewrites them as longer frame delays (`collapseGifHolds` is on by default; the report's `collapse` block shows frames and bytes saved).
- **Stop perpetual churn.** Confetti without `burstFrames`, unbounded particle fields, and never-settling springs trip `TM_PARTICLE_CHURN` and `TM_TRANSITION_UNSETTLED`. Finite bursts are the doctrine: a GIF that never stops moving never compresses.
- **Fix unintended layout shifts.** `TM_LAYOUT_SHIFT` names the culprit sibling and the delta — counting digits need `tabular-nums` or `minWidth`, late siblings need reserved space.
- **Use `--still` for static surfaces.** When the destination is a single frame (link previews, avatars), `renderStill` emits one PNG instead of an animation.

## 4. Pick the leanest surface that works

| Preset | Size | fps | Formats | Budget |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readme-lean` | 850×200 | 12 | gif | 1.25 MiB |
| `readme` | 850×200 | 20 | gif, webp | 2 MiB |
| `readme-hd` | 850×200 | 20 | webp (dpr 2) | 2 MiB |
| `readme-profile` | 850×300 | 20 | gif, webp | 2.25 MiB |
| `readme-wide` | 1280×300 | 20 | gif, webp | 3 MiB |
| `og-card` | 1200×630 | 20 | gif, webp | 4 MiB |

Drop to `readme-lean` when the host platform re-compresses your asset anyway. For sprite-sheet or frame-sequence workflows, the PNG encoder's min-SAD filter heuristic already cut atlas bytes by 90%+ in the v1.0 pass — see [Performance & Size](/explanation/performance-and-size).

<Aside type="note">
  High-chroma OKLCH color sweeps on large areas dither into palette noise in GIFs at dpr 1. The perceptual color API is still the right authoring surface — pair it with WebP when the design demands vivid washes.
</Aside>

### Render Raw HTML
Source: /guides/render-from-raw-html

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The engine accepts raw HTML as a first-class source. Use this path when the animation already exists as markup — a design system snippet, a generated template, a no-JS pipeline — and you need the same deterministic outputs the React path produces.

## Render an HTML string

<Code lang="ts" code={`import { renderHtmlAnimation } from "takumi-motion";

const report = await renderHtmlAnimation({
        html: \`<div id="badge"><h1>ship it</h1></div>\`,
        css: \`
    #badge { display: flex; align-items: center; height: 200px; }
    h1 { opacity: 0; animation: rise 1.2s ease-out forwards; }
    @keyframes rise { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-24px); } to { opacity: 1; } }
        \`,
        frames: 30,
        fps: 20,
        width: 850,
        height: 200,
        outDir: "./out",
});`} />

`renderHtmlAnimation` extracts the `<body>` from full documents (or takes a fragment), hoists `<style>` blocks, samples `frames` deterministic poses of the CSS animations, and encodes the preset formats. The report carries `cssEntries`, `styleBlocksHoisted`, `files`, `posters`, `fonts`, and budget fields.

## Use the CLI for files

The `render` command accepts `.html` and `.htm` files directly:

<Code lang="sh" code={`npx takumi-motion render badge.html --css badge.css --font-file Brand.ttf --frames 40 --out ./out`} />

| Flag | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `--css <file>` | Attach an external stylesheet |
| `--font-file <path>` | Register a local TTF/OTF (repeatable; family defaults to the file stem) |
| `--frames <n>` | Frame count for the HTML path (default 30) |
| `--width` / `--height` / `--dpr` | Surface overrides |
| `--format gif,webp,apng` | Output formats |
| `--budget <bytes>` | Byte budget with exit code 2 on failure |

## Keep determinism intact

- Avoid JavaScript in the HTML — the engine renders markup and CSS, not scripts.
- Font bytes belong in the build: vendor TTF/OTF files locally (`--font-file`) instead of Google Fonts URLs. Remote fonts trip the `TM_FONT_NETWORK` lint because byte-determinism holds only while the remote bytes do.
- WOFF/WOFF2 files are rejected — convert to TTF or OTF first.

## Stills from HTML

`renderStill` accepts the same source trio — react banner, html, or declarative node+timeline:

<Code lang="ts" code={`import { renderStill } from "takumi-motion";

const still = await renderStill({ html: fragment, css, width: 1200, height: 630 });
console.log(still.png.length); // PNG bytes`} />

<LinkCard title="Preview and Inspect" href="/guides/preview-and-inspect" description="Filmstrips and storyboards for HTML and React sources." />

### Seamless Loops
Source: /guides/seamless-loops

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

A looping README badge shows its cut point every few seconds unless the last frame equals the first. Takumi Motion guarantees that equality byte-for-byte instead of asking you to eyeball it. Use this guide whenever you set `<Banner loop>`.

## React path: wrap the seam

Declare `loop` on the banner and mark the boundary that closes the circle. Either the first scene enters with `wrap` or the last scene exits with `wrap` — one of the two, never both:

<Code lang="tsx" code={`<Banner loop fps={24}>
    <Scene duration={90}>…</Scene>
    <Scene duration={76} exit="wrap">…</Scene>
</Banner>`} />

`exit="wrap"` appends a crossfade tail into scene 1's frozen frame-0 layer; at the final wrap frame the leaving node drops, so the last frame and frame 0 are byte-identical by construction. The report carries the verdict:

<Code lang="json" code={`{ "seam": { "mode": "exact", "loop": true } }`} />

<Aside type="caution">
  A `<Banner loop>` without a wrap earns the `TM_LOOP_SEAM` lint pointing at the fix. A `wrap` transition is honored only on the last scene of a looping banner.
</Aside>

Looping banners default their poster to frame 0 — the landing frame — instead of the mid-timeline default.

## Declarative path: loop utilities

The root export includes four composable utilities:

| Utility | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `fadeWrap(timeline, { selector, inMs, outMs, periodMs })` | Owns a target's opacity: fades in, holds, fades out. Sets `timeline.wrap = { selector }` so the seam checker knows the loop is wrapped. Throws when the target already has an opacity track. |
| `alignLoopPeriod(timeline, capMs?)` | Snaps the duration up to the least common multiple of all infinite tracks' periods so every track lands on its phase at the seam. Throws on phase-shifted infinite tracks or an LCM above the cap. |
| `checkLoopSeam(timeline, { tolerance? })` | Returns `{ seamless, mode, diffs }`. `wrapped` mode checks wrap opacity at both ends (tolerance default 0.02); `strict` mode demands every numeric track's first value equal its last. |
| `assertAmbientPeriod(durationMs, periodMs, label)` | Verifies a mirror-cycle ambient track (2× iteration) divides the loop period exactly. |

A complete declarative loop:

<Code lang="ts" code={`import { createTimeline, alignLoopPeriod, fadeWrap, renderBanner } from "takumi-motion";

const timeline = createTimeline({ fps: 20 })
    .add(node, { y: [0, -12, 0] }, { duration: 1200, repeat: Infinity, repeatType: "mirror" });

const aligned = alignLoopPeriod(timeline);
const wrapped = fadeWrap(aligned, { selector: "#badge", inMs: 350, outMs: 350 });

const report = await renderBanner({ node, timeline: wrapped, outDir: "./out" });`} />

## Verify before shipping

- **React path** — read `report.seam.mode`; the golden composition test proves `mode: "exact"` after a byte check.
- **Declarative path** — call `checkLoopSeam(wrapped)` and assert `seamless === true`.
- **CLI** — `takumi-motion check banner.tsx` fails (exit 1) when a declared loop reports `seam.mode === "differs"`. Wire it into CI with [Quality Gates](/guides/ci-quality-gates).

## Reference

API surface: CLI, components, hooks, engine, renderers, lint codes.

### CLI
Source: /reference/cli

import { Aside, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The `takumi-motion` binary ships with the package (`pnpm exec takumi-motion`, `npx takumi-motion`, or `node_modules/.bin/takumi-motion`). Running it with no arguments prints usage and exits with code 1.

## Commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `render <file>` | Render a TS/TSX/JS banner module or an `.html` file to GIF/WebP/APNG, posters, stills, sequences, or sprite sheets |
| `check <file>` | Extent audit + loop-seam + optional size probe — the CI gate (exit 0 pass, 1 fail) |
| `preview <file>` | Write a standalone HTML player of the captured CSS |
| `storyboard <file.tsx>` | Labeled PNG contact sheet of the timeline (React banners) |
| `init [dir]` | Scaffold a `banner.ts` (or `banner.tsx` with `--react`) and a `tsconfig.json`; refuses when a banner file already exists |
| `templates` | List the built-in recipes (`typewriter`, `countup`, `sweep`, `cascade`) |
| `presets` | List presets with size, fps, formats, and budget |
| `fonts` | List the curated Google Font catalog by role |

## Module shapes `render` accepts

The loader resolves each candidate as `mod.default ?? mod.banner ?? mod.element`, then routes by shape:

| Shape | Route |
| --- | --- |
| React element (has `$$typeof`) | React runtime |
| `defineBanner()`-marked function | React runtime |
| Plain sync/async function | Called and awaited; result routed to react or declarative by shape (force react with `--react`) |
| `{ timeline, element \| node, fonts? }` | Declarative path |
| `.html` / `.htm` file | Raw HTML path (pair with `--css`, `--font-file`) |

## Flags

### Surface

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--preset <name>` | `readme` | Preset recipe; explicit surface flags win over it |
| `--width`, `--height` | preset | Logical canvas size in px |
| `--dpr <n>` | preset | Device pixel ratio (surface ceiling: 8192 px, dpr ≤ 8) |
| `--background <color>` | theme | CSS color or `transparent` for an alpha canvas |
| `--fps <n>` | preset | Sampling and encoder fps |

### Output

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--out`, `-o <dir>` | `./out` | Output directory (`preview` honors an `.html` path) |
| `--format <list>` | preset | Comma-separated: `gif,webp,apng` |
| `--quality <0-100>` | preset | WebP quality (mutually exclusive with `--lossless`) |
| `--lossless` | false | Lossless WebP |
| `--no-poster` | false | Skip the poster PNG |
| `--still [frame]` | false | Single-frame PNG instead of an animation (default frame: settled ~60%) |
| `--sequence` | false | PNG frame sequence + `frames.json` manifest |
| `--spritesheet` | false | Sprite atlas PNG + metadata JSON |
| `--sprite-columns <n>` | `ceil(√n)` | Atlas columns |
| `--sprite-every <n>` | 1 | Frame stride in the atlas |
| `--filmstrip [n\|f1,f2,…]` | false | Engine-exact contact sheet next to the outputs |
| `--preview` | false | Also write `banner-preview.html` |
| `--json` | false | Full report as JSON (buffers rendered as `<n bytes>`) |
| `--quiet`, `-q` | false | Suppress the report |

### Budget, data, and execution

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--budget <bytes>` | unset | Budget verdict; triggers the fps ladder (100% → 75% → 50%, floor 6 fps); exit 2 when over |
| `--data <file>` | – | JSON data channel, read once at setup |
| `--font-file <path>` | `[]` | Local TTF/OTF to register (repeatable; family = file stem) |
| `--concurrency <n>` | cores, cap 8 | Bounded parallelism for parse/measure/frame stages |
| `--workers <n\|auto>` | unset (1) | Worker threads for the capture stage (module banners only) |
| `--from <n>` / `--to <n>` | 0 / all | Output-frame window `[from, to)` (React path) |
| `--react` | false | Force the React runtime for unmarked function exports |
| `--kit` | false | Full declarative asset set (`readme`, `readme-hd`, `readme-lean` + static twin) |
| `--explain` | false | Per-frame channel attribution X-ray (React path) |
| `--duration <frames>` | 30 | Frames for the HTML path |
| `--css <file>` | – | Stylesheet for the HTML path |

## Exit codes

| Code | Raised by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | all commands | Success (`check`: "OK — ship it") |
| `1` | all commands | Error or failed audit (`check`: "FAILED — do not ship") |
| `2` | `render --budget`, `--kit` | Output exceeded the byte budget after the ladder |

<Aside type="note">
  `check` prints extents findings per frame (warn for decorative overflow, FAIL for content), the seam verdict, and lint warnings — the same data the JSON report carries.
</Aside>

### Core Engine API
Source: /reference/core-engine

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The root export (`takumi-motion`) exposes the authoring and evaluation core. React is an optional peer — everything on this page runs without it.

## Timelines

### `createTimeline(options?)` → `Timeline`

<Code lang="ts" code={`const timeline = createTimeline({ fps: 20, defaultTransition })
    .add(target, keyframes, options)
    .label("intro");`} />

`add(target, keyframes, options?)` accepts partial records of `AnimatableProperty` → keyframes and returns `TimelineTarget` handles. Options:

| Option | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | `number \| "<" \| "<+n" \| "<-n" \| label` | end of previous | Position on the timeline |
| `stagger` | `number` | `0` | Offset per target (ms) |
| `times` | `number[]` | even | Keyframe times |
| `delay`, `repeat`, `repeatType`, `repeatDelay` | playback | – | `repeatType: "loop" \| "reverse" \| "mirror"` |
| transition fields | – | – | `type`, `stiffness`, `damping`, `duration`, `ease`, … |

Default transitions mirror Motion: more than 2 keyframes → tween 800 ms; transforms → spring (scale 550/damped, others 500/25); everything else → tween 300 ms `ease [0.25, 0.1, 0.35, 1]`. React element targets get auto-assigned `tm-N` selector classes.

`Timeline.toJSON()` produces the interchange format every renderer accepts:

<Code lang="ts" code={`interface TimelineJSON {
    version: 1;
    durationMs: number;
    tracks: TrackJSON[];
    wrap?: { selector: string };
}`} />

### Transforms

| Function | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `shiftTimeline(timeline, deltaMs)` | Moves everything later; refuses negative deltas (they would clip tracks) |
| `concatTimelines([a, b, c])` | Stacks timelines back-to-back — the data equivalent of `<Series.Sequence>` |
| `scaleTimeline(timeline, tempo)` | Rescales tween durations (springs are not rescaled) |

## Compilation and evaluation

### `compileTimeline(json, { fps? = 30, resolveBase?, lint? = true })` → `CompiledTimeline`

Bakes the whole timeline onto a shared fps grid and structural boundaries: CSS keyframes rules per selector, transform props merged per target, linear timing, fill both. Returns `{ css, durationMs, fps, animations, lint }` — `durationMs` is fps-grid aligned; `lint` carries authoring warnings. Renderers call this internally; bake it yourself to inspect or ship the CSS.

### `evaluateAt(json, tMs, { resolveBase?, rawTransforms? })` → `EvaluatedStyles`

Samples every track at time `tMs` and returns `Record<selector, Record<prop, value>>` with the composed `transform` string. This is the single-frame truth the still/filmstrip paths build on. Engine time is integer milliseconds at the boundary (`toEngineMs` clamps and floors).

## Springs and inertia

### `springGenerator(options)` → `SpringGenerator`

| Option | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stiffness` | `100` | Physics mode |
| `damping` | `10` | Physics mode |
| `mass` | `1` | Physics mode |
| `duration` | `800` | Time mode (ms) |
| `bounce` | `0.3` | Time mode (0 = critically damped) |
| `visualDuration` | – | Perceptual duration (s) — alternative to `duration` |
| `velocity` | `0` | Initial velocity |
| `restSpeed` / `restDelta` | Motion defaults | Settle thresholds |
| `keyframes` | – | `[from, to]` for retargetable springs |

The generator exposes `next(t)`, `velocity(t)`, `retarget(keyframes, newVelocity)`, and `calculatedDuration`. Overdamped configurations clamp (`overshootClamping`). Helpers: `calcGeneratorDuration(gen)`, `springDefaults`.

### `inertiaGenerator(options)` → `InertiaGenerator`

Decay-and-bounce motion: `velocity` 0, `power` 0.8, `timeConstant` 325, `bounceDamping` 10, `bounceStiffness` 500, `restDelta` 0.5, optional `min`/`max`/`modifyTarget`. Boundary catch springs keep motion inside the range.

<Aside type="caution">
  Springs are solved by physics — a `duration` on a spring track is silently ignored and trips the `TM_SPRING_DURATION` lint.
</Aside>

## Easing

`Easing` namespace — React Native semantics, exact:

- Curves: `linear`, `easeIn/Out/InOut`, `circIn/Out/InOut`, `backIn/Out/InOut`, `bounceIn/Out/InOut`, `anticipate`
- Factories: `Easing.poly(n)`, `Easing.elastic(bounciness = 1)`, `Easing.back(s = 1.70158)`, `Easing.bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)`, `Easing.steps(n, "start" | "end")`
- Combinators: `Easing.in(f)`, `Easing.out(f)`, `Easing.inOut(f)` — base curves are in-shaped, so `in` is the identity

String names (`"backOut"`, `"easeInOut"`, …) are accepted wherever an `Easing` appears; arrays are cubic beziers. `easingToCssTiming(def)` returns a CSS timing function or `null` when the curve must be baked per-frame. `getEasingForSegment(easing, i)` wraps arrays across segments.

## Interpolation and color

| Function | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `createTweenSampler({ keyframes, times?, ease?, duration }, baseValue?)` | Per-segment easings precomputed, binary-search segment lookup (v1.0); `sample(tMs)` clamps |
| `mixColor(from, to, t, { space? = "oklch" })` | Perceptual mix — **OKLCH is the default**, shortest hue path |
| `interpolateColorFor(frame, inputFrames, colors, { space?, easing? })` | Multi-stop color mapping for the frame |
| `parseColor(css)` / `rgbaToCss(rgba)` / `colorToOklch(css)` | Hex 3/4/6/8, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, 148 named colors, `transparent`; parse results memoize |
| `mixColors` / `mixComplex` / `mixValues` | The frozen compile-path blenders — byte-determinism contract; use `color.ts` APIs for new work |
| `buildTransform` / `isTransformProp` / `transformPropOrder` | CSS transform composition in engine order |

## Next steps

<LinkCard title="Renderers & Reports" href="/reference/renderers" description="Where TimelineJSON goes once authored." />

<LinkCard title="Architecture" href="/explanation/architecture" description="How authoring, compiling, and rasterizing connect." />

### Hooks & Motion Math
Source: /reference/hooks

import { Aside, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Hooks read the frame context inside `<Scene>` (they throw outside one). Each hook has a pure companion — the same math taking the frame explicitly — importable from the root export for use outside React.

## Frame context

| Hook | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `useFrame()` | `FrameInfo { frame, absolute, sceneFrames, bannerFrames, fps, timeMs }` |
| `useCurrentFrame()` | Scene-local frame (restarts per scene) |
| `useAbsoluteFrame()` | Global banner frame |
| `useDuration()` | Current scene's duration in frames |
| `useFps()` | Banner fps |
| `useCue(expr)` | Absolute frame for a cue expression: `"intro"`, `"intro+12f"` (scenes need a `label`) |

## Springs and interpolation

| Hook | Signature | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `useSpring` | `(options?: SpringAtOptions) => number` | Spring sampled at the current frame |
| `useStaggeredSpring` | `(index, options?: StaggeredSpringOptions) => number` | Spring delayed by `startFrames + index × intervalFrames` (defaults 0/2) |
| `useInterpolate` | `(inputFrames, output, easing?) => number` | Eased multi-stop mapping, clamped |
| `usePulse` | `(periodFrames) => number` | Triangle 0→1→0, frame-aligned |
| `useSmoothPulse` | `(periodFrames) => number` | Sine 0→1→0 |

Spring options carry Motion's full vocabulary: `stiffness` (100), `damping` (10), `mass` (1), `duration` (800), `bounce` (0.3), `visualDuration`, `velocity`, `restSpeed`, `restDelta`, `overshootClamping`, plus `from` (0), `to` (1), `delayFrames` (0).

`SpringAtOptions` fields may be functions of the frame index for per-frame retargeting.

## Pure companions (root export)

| Function | Signature | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `springFor` | `(frame, fps, options) => number` | Memoized solver (v1.0 Velocity) |
| `interpolateFor` | `(frame, inputFrames, output, easing?) => number` | Hook-free `useInterpolate` |
| `interpolate` | `(input, inputRange, outputRange, { easing?, extrapolateLeft?, extrapolateRight? })` | Remotion-signature mapping; monotonic, equal-length ranges |
| `pulseFor` / `smoothPulseFor` | `(frame, periodFrames) => number` | Hook-free pulses |
| `randomFor` | `(seed, ...salt) => number` | mulberry32-derived value in `[0, 1)`, stable per (seed, salt) |
| `noiseFor` | `(seed, options?) => number` | 2D value noise in ± amplitude (amp 1, frequency 0.1) |
| `staggerDelay` / `staggeredSpringFor` | `(index, ...) => ...` | Hook-free stagger |
| `springPresets` | `snappy`, `bouncy`, `gentle`, `wobbly`, `stiff`, `slow` | Spread into any spring: `useSpring({ ...springPresets.snappy, from: 24 })` |
| `springSettleFrames` | `(fps, options) => number` | Frames until the spring rests — `Infinity` for absurd configs |
| `wiggleFor` | `(seed, frame, { amplitude=4, frequency=0.15 }) => number` | Hook-free `<Wiggle>` |
| `frameToMs` / `msToFrames` | `(n, fps) => number` | `msToFrames` rounds up |
| `mulberry32` | `(seed) => () => number` | The seeded PRNG underpinning all randomness |
| `hashString` | `(s) => number` | String → numeric seed |

## State and data

| Hook | Signature | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `useFrameState` | `(reducer, initial, events?) => S` | State replayed from frame 0 on every render — the reducer must be deterministic; `events(frame)` returns actions or null |
| `useChartData` | `<T>(hint?) => T` | The banner data object; throws with a key hint when absent |
| `hasChartData` | `() => boolean` | Quiet check |
| `useEntering` / `useExiting` | `(descriptor) => { opacity?, transform? } \| null` | `null` = settled = emit nothing |

## Canonical names, intentionally distinct

| Purpose | Canonical | Hook sugar | Pure companion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Frame-range mapping | `interpolate(frame, in, out, { easing })` | `useInterpolate(in, out, easing?)` | `interpolateFor(frame, in, out, easing?)` |
| Spring | `useSpring(options)` | — | `springFor(frame, fps, options)` |
| Stagger | `useStaggeredSpring(index, opts)` | — | `staggeredSpringFor(...)` |

The three interpolate variants are intentionally distinct: context-free vs context-reading. Prefer `interpolate` for new code.

<Aside type="caution">
  Never call `Math.random()` in a render function. Use `useRandom`/`randomFor` (seeded) — that is what makes frames replay byte-identically and what lets worker windows merge byte-exactly.
</Aside>

<LinkCard title="Determinism" href="/explanation/determinism" description="Why seeded randomness and integer engine time are non-negotiable." />

### Lint Codes
Source: /reference/lint-codes

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Every render (`renderReactBanner`, `renderBanner`, `renderWithAudit`) carries a `lint: LintWarning[]` channel alongside the legacy `warnings: string[]`. Findings are deduplicated, capped at 20 per code (with a truncation notice), and survive `--json` — a consumer platform can render them, filter them, or fail CI on specific codes.

<Code lang="ts" code={`interface LintWarning {
    code: LintCode;   // stable TM_* identifier
    message: string;  // diagnosis, with the offending key/value/path
    hint?: string;    // the fix, phrased as what to do instead
    severity: "warn" | "info";
}`} />

## Style safety

| Code | Catches | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TM_KEBAB_STYLE` | Kebab-case keys in React style objects | React 19's unitless table is keyed on camelCase — `"font-weight": 700` renders as `font-weight:700px`, which the engine rejects (render fails with a Rust parse error). Fix: `"fontWeight"` |
| `TM_NAN_STYLE` | `NaN` / `Infinity` / `undefined` in styles or markup | Broken springs (stiffness 0), inverted interpolate ranges — silently produces garbage styles |
| `TM_EMPTY_STYLE` | Elements that rendered `style=""` | Every declaration was dropped upstream — usually the kebab bug or an undefined style object |
| `TM_UNKNOWN_STYLE_PROP` | (strict mode) properties outside `SUPPORTED_STYLE_PROPS` | Advisory — the engine supports more than the curated list; verify then extend |

Type-level safety pairs with the lint: `satisfies TakumiStyle` turns typos into compile errors, `UNITLESS_STYLE_PROPS` mirrors React's unitless table, and `--custom` properties go through the explicit `--*` key form.

## Motion and layout

| Code | Catches | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TM_SPRING_DURATION` | Declarative tracks mixing `type: "spring"` with `duration` | Springs are solved by physics; the duration is silently ignored |
| `TM_TRANSITION_UNSETTLED` | `<Animated>` enter/exit that cannot complete inside its scene window | Settling math is in the message; check `springSettleFrames(fps, opts) <= framesRemaining` for raw `useSpring` |
| `TM_LAYOUT_SHIFT` | A measured box that moves inside a scene without an authored transform | The culprit sibling and delta are named. Fix: absolute park, reserved space, or fixed-width digits (`tabular-nums`, `minWidth`) |
| `TM_MORPH_UNMEASURED` | `<Morph>` without prewarmed rects | Items jump — render through the capture runtime, which prewarms both layout states |
| `TM_FITTEXT_UNMEASURED` | `<FitText>` without a prewarmed measurement | Fell back to `max` font size — render through the runtime or precompute with `fitFontSize()` |
| `TM_NOISE_ALIASED` | Noise frequency above 0.5 lattice cells/frame (Nyquist) | Motion aliases into strobing — `<Camera shake>`, `<Wiggle>` |
| `TM_VELOCITY_DROPPED` | `carryVelocity()` requested on a segment that cannot receive it | The chain loses momentum silently otherwise |

## Size and output

| Code | Catches | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TM_GLOW_GIF_DITHER` | `filter: blur()` in a GIF render at dpr 1 | Palette dithering of soft gradients is the leading GIF size trap — 1× glow GIFs compressed worse than 2× in benchmarks. Prefer WebP, dpr 2, or flat accents |
| `TM_PARTICLE_CHURN` | Unbounded particle churn or confetti without `burstFrames` / over the 24-particle budget | Size is per-frame delta × frames; a field that never settles never compresses |
| `TM_LOOP_SEAM` | A `<Banner loop>` whose last frame differs from frame 0 (no `wrap`) | The loop visibly snaps — the hint points at `exit="wrap"` |
| `TM_FONT_NETWORK` | Google Font specs or URL font files fetched at render | Byte-determinism holds only while the remote bytes do — vendor TTF/OTF locally |

## Working with the channel

<Code lang="ts" code={`const report = await renderReactBanner({ banner: MyBanner });

for (const warning of report.lint) {
    console.log(\`[\${warning.severity}] \${warning.code}: \${warning.message}\`);
    if (warning.hint) console.log(\`  fix: \${warning.hint}\`);
}`} />

Helpers: `collectLintWarnings` dedupes, `formatLint` renders text, `camelHint` produces the kebab→camel suggestion, `NO_LINT` is the empty channel. Strict mode (unknown-property checking) is opt-in per lint call.

<Aside type="tip">
  The lint is advisory — nothing fails a render by itself. Gate on it by filtering specific codes in CI, or use `takumi-motion check` for the hard-fail audits (extents, seam, budget).
</Aside>

### Package Exports
Source: /reference/package-exports

import { Aside, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`takumi-motion` is ESM (`"type": "module"`), types included. React is an optional peer dependency — import the core without it.

## Subpath map

| Import | Exposes |
| --- | --- |
| `takumi-motion` | Everything: core engine (timelines, compile, evaluate, springs, easings, color), renderers (`renderBanner`, `renderReactBanner`, `renderStill`, …), the React runtime re-export, audit, fonts, themes, presets, templates, lint, surface, concurrency, storyboard, filmstrip, kit |
| `takumi-motion/react` | The authoring surface: primitives (`Banner`, `Scene`, `Layer`), sequencing (`Sequence`, `Freeze`, `Series`, `Loop`), hooks, motion math, `SplitText`, `Fill`/`Img`/`FitText`, material pack, charts, `<Morph>`, `<Particles>`, `<Animated>`/`<Keyframes>`, `<Camera>`/`<Wiggle>`/`<FollowPath>`, enter/exit vocabulary, `chain`/`hold`, cue system, data channel |
| `takumi-motion/audit` | `renderWithAudit` + audit types — the embeddability contract for platforms rendering user banners |
| `takumi-motion/fonts` | `ensureFonts`, `fontCatalog`, `fontStack`, `isCatalogFont`, `loadedFontFamilies` |
| `takumi-motion/recipes` | The four template builders, `bannerTemplates`, `buildTemplate` |
| `takumi-motion/kit` | `CountUp`, `Typewriter`, `Glow` + number-pattern helpers |

The binary is `takumi-motion` (`package.json` → `bin`), mapped to the compiled CLI.

## Runtime requirements

| Requirement | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | 22+ (developed against 24) |
| Engine | `@takumi-rs/core` ≥ 2.17 (peer `@takumi-rs/helpers` ≥ 2.17.0) — the Rust rasterizer arrives as a prebuilt native module |
| React | 19 (optional peer) |
| Fonts | takumi bundles Geist Latin by default; register anything else through the fonts API |

## Types worth knowing

| Type | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| `TimelineJSON` | `{ version: 1, durationMs, tracks: TrackJSON[], wrap? }` — the interchange format |
| `AnimationFormat` | `"gif" \| "webp" \| "apng"` |
| `BannerPreset` | A full surface recipe (width, height, dpr, fps, formats, quality, budget) |
| `SurfaceSpec` | `{ width, height, dpr, fps, formats, quality, lossless, background, budgetBytes }` |
| `TakumiStyle` | The typed, engine-verified style property set (`+` explicit `--*` custom props) |
| `LintWarning` | `{ code, message, hint?, severity }` |
| `ReactBannerReport` | The full render report — see [Renderers & Reports](/reference/renderers) |

<Aside type="note">
  Import types with `import type { TimelineJSON } from "takumi-motion"` — the type surface is part of the public contract and versioned with the changelog.
</Aside>

<LinkCard title="React Components" href="/reference/react-components" description="The authoring surface behind the /react export." />

### Presets, Themes & Fonts
Source: /reference/presets-and-themes

import { Aside, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Presets are recipes, not constraints — every field they set (width, height, dpr, fps, formats, quality, background, budget) can be overridden per render, and explicit options win.

## Banner presets

| Name | Size | dpr | fps | Formats | WebP quality | Budget |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readme` | 850×200 | 1 | 20 | gif, webp | 82 | 2 MiB |
| `readme-hd` | 850×200 | 2 | 20 | webp | 82 | 2 MiB |
| `readme-lean` | 850×200 | 1 | 12 | gif | 78 | 1.25 MiB |
| `readme-profile` | 850×300 | 1 | 20 | gif, webp | 82 | 2.25 MiB |
| `readme-wide` | 1280×300 | 1 | 20 | gif, webp | 82 | 3 MiB |
| `og-card` | 1200×630 | 1 | 20 | gif, webp | 85 | 4 MiB |

Surface engine defaults: dpr 1, fps 30, formats `[gif, webp]`, quality 82, budget 4 MiB. Hard limits: dimension ceiling 8192 px, dpr ≤ 8, fps ≤ 120. `resolveSurface(spec, preset?)` and `resolveBackground()` implement the rules; `deviceSize()` converts logical to device pixels.

## Themes

Seven built-in themes, resolved over `midnight` when partial:

| Name | Character |
| --- | --- |
| `midnight` | Default — deep blue-black, calm accent |
| `github-dark` / `github-light` | GitHub palette pair |
| `tokyo-night` | Blue-violet on dark (accent `#7aa2f7`, font Sora) |
| `dracula` | Classic Dracula purples and pinks |
| `sunburst` | Warm light theme |
| `paper-mono` | Monochrome paper look |

A `Theme` carries `{ name, bg, text, textDim, textFaint, surface, surfaceBorder, accent, glow, font? }`. Pass a partial object as `ThemeInput` to customize — missing fields complete from `midnight`.

## Font catalog

`ensureFonts(renderer, specs)` registers Google Fonts by name (deduped per renderer); `fontCatalog` groups the curated list:

| Role | Families |
| --- | --- |
| display | Space Grotesk, Sora, Outfit, Manrope, Archivo, Inter |
| mono | JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Mono, Space Mono, Fira Code |
| serif | Playfair Display, Lora, Fraunces |
| body | Inter, Manrope, Noto Sans |

A `FontSpec` is a family name or `{ name, weight?, style?, generic? }`. Variable fonts register with a range: `{ name: "Inter", weight: "100..900" }` — required for `<VariableText>`.

For reproducible builds, vendor files locally: `loadFontFiles` accepts paths, URLs, or `Uint8Array` (TTF/OTF only — WOFF/WOFF2 are rejected). Remote fonts work but trip `TM_FONT_NETWORK` because byte-determinism holds only while the remote bytes do.

## Personalities

Personality presets drive easing curves, stagger, hold bias, and ambient intensity for templates and orchestration helpers:

| Name | Entrance | Stagger | Ambient |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `snappy` | backOut, spring 520/26 | 28 ms | 0.8 |
| `smooth` | easeInOut | 42 ms | 0.6 |
| `playful` | backOut/circIn, spring 300/17 | 34 ms | 1.0 |
| `mechanical` | steps(8, end) / steps(6, start) | even 22 ms | 0.35 |

Ambient motion helpers: `ambient(timeline, target, kind, { periodMs, intensity })` adds a mirror-cycle track (`kind: "drift" | "breathe" | "pulse" | "float"` — periods must divide the loop period exactly); `ambientWindow(...)` freezes holds between active windows. Orchestration: `splitGlyphs`, `splitWords`, `revealUnits`, `revealRow`, `waveUnits`, `deceleratingStagger`.

## Banner templates

The `takumi-motion/recipes` export ships four strict-seam recipes — `typewriter`, `countup`, `sweep`, `cascade` — each an async builder returning a `BannerResult { element, timeline, fonts? }`. Shared props: `theme`, `motion`, `font`, `width=850`, `height=200`, `fps=20`, `renderer?`.

| Template | Own props (defaults) | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `typewriter` | `text` (required), `tagline?`, `accent?`, `background?`, `speed=65` ms/char, `startMs=300`, `holdMs=1500` | Type-in with per-char fade, hold, terminal backspace, blink tail; strict loop |
| `countup` | `stats` (required: `{ label, value, suffix?, decimals? }[]`), `title?`, `accent?`, `background?`, `steps=6`, `countMs=1200`, `startMs=450`, `holdMs=1800` | Digit-layer crossfade stat columns |
| `sweep` | `title` (required), `subtitle?`, `secondaryColor="#22d3ee"`, `background?`, `accent?`, `holdMs=1900` | Gradient glow sweep + letter-tracking entrance, fade-out exit |
| `cascade` | `title` (required), `tagline?`, `accent?`, `background?`, `startMs=260`, `holdMs=1700`, `rise=20` (0..48) | Per-glyph rise+fade with decelerating stagger, accent-rule overshoot, cascade exit |

`buildTemplate({ name, props })` invokes by name; `bannerTemplates` lists the registry.

<Aside type="note">
  Template results already carry their fonts and theme — pass the whole result to `renderBanner` or the CLI and the renderer registers everything before measuring.
</Aside>

<LinkCard title="Renderers & Reports" href="/reference/renderers" description="How presets resolve at render time." />

### React Components
Source: /reference/react-components

import { Aside, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

All components import from `takumi-motion/react` (the kinetic kit also from `takumi-motion/kit`). Every component is a pure function of the current frame — no clocks, no `Math.random`.

## Structure

### `<Banner>`

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | `string \| BannerPreset` | `"readme"` | Surface recipe |
| `width`, `height` | `number` | preset | Logical canvas overrides |
| `dpr` | `number` | preset | Device pixel ratio |
| `background` | `string \| null` | theme bg | `"transparent"`/`null` → alpha canvas |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` | `"midnight"` | Theme name or partial theme |
| `fps` | `number` | preset fps | Frames per second |
| `fonts` | `FontSpec \| FontSpec[]` | – | Fonts registered before capture |
| `loop` | `boolean` | `false` | Declares a loop; pair with a `wrap` transition |
| `transitionMs` | `number` | `250` | Default scene-transition overlap |
| `tempo` | `number` | `1` | Finite, > 0 — global timeline speedup |

Children must be `<Scene>`, `<Layer>`, or `<Series>` (fragments flatten). At least one scene is required; the maximum is 64.

### `<Scene>`

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `duration` | `number` | required | Frames |
| `enter`, `exit` | `TransitionInput` | `"cut"` | `"cut" \| "crossfade" \| "slide" \| "rise" \| "push" \| "wrap"` or `{ kind, ms }` |
| `label` | `string` | – | Unique; enables `useCue("label+12f")` |

`wrap` is honored only on the last scene of a looping banner. `push` never blends — both sides must declare it.

### `<Layer>`

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `top` | `boolean` | `true` when neither set | Render above the scene stack |
| `bottom` | `boolean` | `false` | Render beneath the scene stack |

## Sequencing

| Component | Props | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<Sequence>` | `from=0`, `durationInFrames` (rest of scope), `speed=1`, `reverse=false` | Children render only inside the window; absolute frame tracking is preserved |
| `<Freeze>` | `at` (required) | Children see frame `at` forever |
| `<Series>` | children only | Flat list of `<Series.Sequence>`; nesting errors |
| `<Series.Sequence>` | `durationInFrames` (required), `enter`/`exit="cut"` | Stacks scenes back-to-back |
| `<Loop>` | `durationInFrames` (required ≥ 1), `times=Infinity`, children or `(iteration) => ReactNode` | Repeats its subtree; also the child's `useDuration` |

## Text and content

| Component | Props (defaults) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<SplitText>` | `text`, `by="chars" \| "words"`, `renderUnit` | Splits into `TextUnit`s `{text, index, total, isSpace}` |
| `<FitText>` | `text`, `maxWidth` (canvas − 32), `fontWeight=400`, `max=64`, `min=18`, `pad=0.985` | Largest engine-measured size that fits; outside the runtime → `max` + `TM_FITTEXT_UNMEASURED` |
| `<Fill>` | `style` | Absolute inset-0 flex container — centering works by default |
| `<Img>` | `src` (string data URI or `Buffer`), `mime="image/png"`, `width`, `height`, `alt`, `style` | Resolve files with `imageDataUriFromFile()` before capture |
| `<CountUp>` | `to`, `from=0`, `durationFrames` (scene), `delayFrames=0`, `spring?`, `ease="easeOut"`, `format` | Pattern grammar: `"$,.0f"`, `",.1f%"`, `"ms"`; `tabular-nums` forced |
| `<Typewriter>` | `text`, `durationFrames` (scene − 12), `delayFrames=0`, `cursor=true`, `cursorPeriodFrames=15`, `cursorColor="currentColor"` | Cursor is an em-sized currentColor block that blinks |
| `<Glow>` | `color="#38bdf8"`, `size=220`, `x=0`, `y=0`, `blur=44`, `opacity=0.14` | Defaults encode the size doctrine; mind `TM_GLOW_GIF_DITHER` |

## Motion vocabulary

| Component | Props (defaults) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<Animated>` | `entering?`, `exiting?`, `style` | Wraps a plain `div`; settles to **no** style overrides |
| `<Keyframes>` | `frames` (`{ [frame]: { ...channels, easing? } }`), `style` | Properties fill forward; colors mix in OKLCH |
| `<Camera>` | `pushIn?`, `pan?`, `shake?`, `transformOrigin?` | `shake` amplitude 3, frequency 0.2 — aliasing above 0.5 trips `TM_NOISE_ALIASED` |
| `<Wiggle>` | `amplitude=4`, `seed`, `rotateAmplitude=0` | Per-frame noise offset |
| `<FollowPath>` | `d`, `durationFrames`, `delayFrames=0`, `easing="easeInOut"`, `rotate={false \| "auto" \| number}` | Moves along an SVG path |
| `<Morph>` | `from`, `to`, `itemIds`, `renderItem`, `switchFrame=0`, `durationFrames=14`, `staggerFrames=0`, `contentSwitchAt=0.5`, `containerStyle?`, `itemStyle?` | Measured FLIP through position+size channels — no scale, no text stretching; unmeasured → `TM_MORPH_UNMEASURED` |
| `<Particles>` | `count=24` (≤ 256), `mode="sparkle" \| "confetti"`, `seed=1`, `colors`, `size`, `area`, `burstFrames?`, `gravity=0.35`, `speed=2.4`, `twinklePeriodFrames=16`, `opacity=0.9` | Closed-form per-frame particles; confetti without `burstFrames` trips `TM_PARTICLE_CHURN` |

Enter/exit presets (26 total, e.g. `FadeInDown`, `ZoomIn`) chain with `.duration(frames)`, `.delay(frames)`, `.springify(presetOrOptions)`; `staggered(preset, index, opts)` bakes stagger; `defineTransition({ name, side, channels, durationFrames, easing })` declares custom ones. Segments compose with `chain(...)` and `hold(frames)`.

## Charts

| Component | Props (defaults) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<LineChart>` | `data?`, `draw="reveal" \| "none"`, `drawDurationFrames=40`, `drawDelayFrames=6`, `area=false`, `grid=true`, `showPoints`, `showLabels`, `yTicks=4`, `strokeWidth=3` | One static SVG + per-frame clip-path sweep |
| `<BarChart>` | `data?`, `orientation="up" \| "right"`, `stagger=true`, `spring`, `showValues=true`, `formatValue`, `showLabels`, `gap=8`, `radius=6` | Bars grow with staggered springs from the measured plot box |
| `<Donut>` | `value` (0..1, required), `size=140`, `thickness=size×0.14`, `color`, `trackColor`, `holeColor`, `paint="transform" \| "conic"`, `drawDurationFrames=36`, `center?` | `transform` is palette-safe; `conic` is the gradient alternative |

Charts read the data channel via `useChartData` when the `data` prop is absent. Data shape: `ChartData = { series: [{ name, color, points }], labels?, max? }`; helpers `niceMax()`, `compactNumber()`.

## Material pack

| Component | Props (defaults) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<Reveal>` | `wipe="left" \| "right" \| "up" \| "down" \| "circle"` (default `"right"`), `drawDurationFrames=30`, `drawDelayFrames=0`, `feather=0` | Animated mask gradient; `feather=0` is palette-safe |
| `<Mask>` | `image?`, `fade="top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right"`, `fadeLength=24`, `mode="alpha" \| "luminance" \| "match-source"` | Exactly one of `image`/`fade` required |
| `<VariableText>` | `text`, `from=300`, `to=800`, `durationFrames=24`, `axis="wght"`, `fontSize?` | Requires a variable font registered with a weight range |
| `<GradientText>` | `text`, `gradient` (linear-gradient), `fontSize?`, `fontWeight?` | Static `background-clip: text` fill |

<Aside type="caution">
  The particles ship as one component: `<Particles mode="sparkle">` and `<Particles mode="confetti">`. There are no `<Sparkle>` or `<Confetti>` elements.
</Aside>

## Next steps

<LinkCard title="Hooks & Motion Math" href="/reference/hooks" description="useFrame, useSpring, useInterpolate, and the pure companions." />

<LinkCard title="Lint Codes" href="/reference/lint-codes" description="What each component can warn about during capture." />

### Renderers & Reports
Source: /reference/renderers

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Every renderer returns a report object — the report is the API. All of them are deterministic: same inputs produce the same bytes at any concurrency and any worker count.

## `renderBanner` — declarative path

<Code lang="ts" code={`const report = await renderBanner({
    node,              // takumi node tree, or a React-shaped element
    timeline,          // TimelineJSON (timeline.toJSON())
    preset: "readme",  // explicit options win over the preset
    outDir: "./out",   // omit to receive buffers only
    baseName: "banner",
});`} />

Key options beyond the surface fields: `formats?`, `fps?`, `posters?` (default one at 60% of the timeline; `false` to skip), `fonts?`, `webpQuality?`/`quality?`, `lossless?`, `budgetBytes?`, `collapseGifHolds?` (default `true`), `sequence?`, `spriteSheet?`, `parallel?` (default `true`).

`BannerReport` fields: `preset`, `width`, `height`, `devicePixelRatio`, `physicalWidth`, `physicalHeight`, `fps`, `frames`, `durationMs`, `files[]` (`{ path, format, bytes, ms, withinBudget, frames, buffer }`), `posters[]`, `collapse` (`framesBefore/After`, `bytesBefore/After`), `fonts`, `totalBytes`, `budgetBytes`, `overBudget`, `warnings`, `surface`, `lint`, `sequence?`, `spriteSheet?`. `formatReport(report)` renders the human-readable text.

## `renderReactBanner` — React path

<Code lang="ts" code={`const report = await renderReactBanner({
    banner: MyBanner,           // or bannerModule: "./banner.tsx" (enables workers)
    workers: "auto",
    formats: ["webp"],
    outDir: "./out",
});`} />

Options: `banner` xor `bannerModule`, `workers?: number | "auto"`, `preset?`, `fps?`, `formats?`, `outDir?`, `baseName?`, `fonts?`, `posters?` (default: frame 0 for loops, else the settled 60% frame), `collapseGifHolds?`, `safeZone?` (8), `sequence?`, `spriteSheet?`, `parallel?`, `concurrency?`, `fromFrame?`/`toFrame?`, `data?`, `explain?: boolean`, plus `SurfaceSpec` fields.

Everything `BannerReport` carries, plus:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `scenes` | Planned scene windows |
| `chunks` | Byte-identical frame chunks after merging |
| `extents` | `{ canvas, safeZonePx, chunksChecked, transitionChunksSkipped, violations[] }` |
| `seam` | `{ mode: "exact" \| "differs", loop }` — byte-checked |
| `timings` | `{ captureMs, parseMs, auditMs, encodeMs, totalMs }` |
| `lint` | Coded warnings (`TM_*`) with hints |
| `window` | The `[from, to)` frame window that ran |
| `explain?` | Per-frame channel attribution when `explain: true` |

## `renderStill` — one PNG, any source

<Code lang="ts" code={`const still = await renderStill({ banner: MyBanner });           // react
const still = await renderStill({ html, css });                  // raw HTML
const still = await renderStill({ node, timeline });             // declarative`} />

Options: `frame?` (default: settled ~60% frame; frame 0 for HTML), `width`/`height`/`dpr`/`fps`, `quality`/`lossless`, `budgetBytes?`, `fonts?`/`fontFiles?`, `outDir?` (writes `<base>.png`), `concurrency?`. Returns `{ source, frame, timeMs, width, height, devicePixelRatio, physicalWidth, physicalHeight, background, png, bytes, ms, path }`.

## `renderSpriteSheet` and `exportFrameSequence`

| Renderer | Options | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `renderSpriteSheet(renderer, source, opts)` | `columns?` (default `ceil(√n)`), `every?` (1), `maxPixels?` (64M), `concurrency?` | Atlas PNG + metadata `{ version, frameWidth, frameHeight, columns, rows, frameCount, fps, frames[], css }` — `meta.css` is a ready-to-paste `steps()` recipe |
| `exportFrameSequence(renderer, source, opts)` | `outDir` (required), `dirName="sequence"`, `every=1`, `baseName="frame"`, `concurrency?` | `frame_00000.png` files + `frames.json` manifest containing an ffmpeg one-liner; identical-frame runs render once and rewrite bytes per file |

## `renderHtmlAnimation` — raw HTML source

<Code lang="ts" code={`const report = await renderHtmlAnimation({
    html,              // fragment or full document (<style> hoisted)
    css?,              // extra stylesheet(s)
    frames: 30,
    outDir: "./out",
});`} />

Returns `HtmlSourceReport` with `surface`, `frames`, `durationMs`, `cssEntries`, `styleBlocksHoisted`, `files`, `posters`, `fonts`, `fontFiles`, `totalBytes`, `budgetBytes`, `overBudget`, `warnings`, `collapse`.

## `renderWithAudit` — audit as data

<Code lang="ts" code={`import { renderWithAudit } from "takumi-motion/audit";

const { report, audit, exitCode, formatted } = await renderWithAudit({
    banner: MyBanner,          // or node+timeline, or html+css
    preset: "readme",
    budgetBytes: 2 * 1024 * 1024,
    outDir: "./out",
});`} />

`AuditReport`: `generator`, `generatorVersion`, `source`, `surface`, `timeline { frames, durationMs }`, `budget { budgetBytes, totalBytes, overBudget, files[] }`, `extents { checked, violations[], hardFailures }`, `seam { mode, loop }`, `determinism { deterministic, checkedBytes, detail }`, `warnings`. Exit codes: `0` pass, `1` content failure, `2` over budget. The determinism probe performs a full second render and byte-compares the first poster.

## `renderKit` — the full asset set

<Code lang="ts" code={`const kit = await renderKit(bannerResult, {
    outDir: "./assets",
    presets: ["readme", "readme-hd", "readme-lean"], // default
});`} />

Returns `KitReport { variants[], files[] ({ path, role }), totalBytes }` and writes `<base>-<preset>.<ext>` plus `banner-static.png` — a reduced-motion twin. The CLI exits 2 when any variant exceeds its budget. Declarative banners only.

## Concurrency primitives

| Function | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `resolveConcurrency(limit?)` | Validated int (cap 64) or `min(availableParallelism(), 8, 64)` |
| `mapWithConcurrency(items, limit, fn)` | Sliding-window map preserving input order |
| `resolveWorkers(option, frameCount, estimatedWorkMs)` | The `"auto"` gate: cores ≥ 4, frames ≥ 128, work ≥ 400 ms; cap 16 |
| `windowGrid(total, workers)` | Even frame windows for the pool |

<Aside type="note">
  Output bytes are identical at any concurrency or worker count — parallelism changes wall-clock time only. The determinism probe in `renderWithAudit` exists to catch impurities that would break that promise.
</Aside>
